**Finding: missing** (INSURANCE — Vendor insurance)

**Investigation:** A full-text search for "insurance" returned zero hits, and I read § 20 General Matters end-to-end (p0135–p0147, subsections (a) through (i)) — it covers time, notices, waiver, assignment, independent contractor, force majeure, severability, governing law and headings, but no insurance covenant. "Customer Data" is not a defined term in this Agreement.

**Why the rule is triggered:** Garman is not a pure remote licensor. It installs the Software on the AS400s at each Authorized Location and remains available for future on-site installations (p0041, p0042), and it converts "Sparkling's data ... from its current electronic form into a form suitable for processing with the Software" (p0042). A vendor that both attends our premises and processes our data with no insurance at all is expressly walk-away territory under this rule, and falls short of even the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M).

**Redline (validated ok:true):** Inserted a new § 20(j) at the preferred position — CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where Garman handles our data, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request, running through the term plus one year. Two drafting adaptations: I used "Sparkling's data" instead of the model language's "Customer Data" since that term is undefined here, and placed the clause in the miscellaneous section per the redline guidance rather than creating a standalone article.

The comment flags E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M as the fallback so the negotiator has a ready concession if Garman pushes back on the cyber limit.
